observation.visible_scene: A dim workshop interior. A man wearing amber-tinted safety glasses and a camouflage-patterned protective jacket/leaning apron is bent over a workbench, holding a handheld power tool against a thin horizontal metal bar/plate. Bright orange-white sparks continuously burst from the tool's contact point and cascade downward in a fan. Background fixtures remain in place: a wall shelf with a green boxy machine, a red fire extinguisher, electrical boxes with looping black cables, and a drill press to the right; a dark lathe headstock occupies the left foreground.
visible_changes: The spark shower is present in every sampled frame but its pattern, density and spread fluctuate from frame to frame (some frames show a tight vertical column, others a wider fan with sparks streaking leftward along the top edge of the bar).
The worker's overall posture stays bent and head-down throughout, with only small adjustments of the head, shoulders and gloved hands around the tool.
The tool-bar contact point remains near the same horizontal location on the bar across the excerpt, with no large lateral travel.
Background objects keep fixed positions relative to the frame edges, so the camera framing is essentially static (no clear pan or zoom).
outside_clip_unknowns: The exact identity of the tool (angle grinder, cut-off wheel, or welder) and the material of the bar.
What occurs before the first frame and after the last frame (the grinding/cutting action is already ongoing at the start and continues past the end).
Whether the bar is being cut, ground, or welded.
uncertain_details: Any slight camera drift is not distinguishable from scene changes given the static background.
The small apparent shifts of the contact point along the bar could be minor tool repositioning rather than deliberate travel.
The cause of the varying spark pattern (tool angle, pressure, or material) cannot be determined from the images.
